newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad opposition to resolve leadership crisis.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad opposition to resolve leadership crisis.

text.p: Trinidad and Tobago's main opposition party will hold a special convention on Sunday to resolve a leadership crisis set off by its defeat in last year's general elections.

Some 775 delegates will decide whether the People's National Movement (PNM) should continue under former prime minister Patrick Manning, who has led the party for nine years, or pick his rival Keith Rowley to replace him.
Trinidadian voters threw Manning out of office after four years last November and since then there have been increasing calls for him to relinquish the party leadership.

Kamaluddin Mohammed, one of the PNM's founders, said the party "has drifted from its moorings and it's time to put it back on course." Mohammed has come out in support of Rowley, a 46-year-old Tobagonian, to lead a new party executive.
Rowley, dubbed "the rottweiler" by Manning, is a geologist by training, as is the former prime minister.
The black-dominated PNM is Trinidad's oldest political organisation and ruled the Caribbean state for 30 successive years after its founding in 1956.
